title: observability-led-cost-and-fidelity-profiling-manual-2026
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Overview
========
This document defines the observability-driven profiling methodology used to measure and correlate runtime telemetry with operator cost and model fidelity. It is a cross-cutting manual intended for runtime engineers, SREs, and applied-ML teams who run fidelity-sensitive experiments, kernel scheduling changes, or cost optimizations (batching, quantization, caching). The goal is repeatable, low-noise profiling that produces actionable signal for rollouts and release gates.

Scope and goals
----------------
- Scope: production-like inference runtime across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.
- Goals:
  - Produce a repeatable experiment matrix that ties telemetry signals to per-token cost and fidelity deltas.
  - Provide a step-by-step runbook for incident-driven profiling and change verification.
  - Define an instrumentation contract for kernel schedulers and runtime components so signals are comparable across environments.
  - Integrate profiling outputs with the benchmarking suite and release gates.

Ownership and roles
-------------------
- Document owner: eng-serving-runtime observability group.
- Primary engineers: runtime-observability (oncall), kernel-scheduler team, profiling-lab.
- Reviewers: applied-ml (for fidelity metrics), cost-analytics (for cost-per-token alignment).

Key definitions and success metrics
----------------------------------
- Fidelity delta: measurable change in model output quality for a fixed prompt set (see fidelity prompts in the benchmarking suite). Expressed as a percent regression or score delta (ex: BLEU, embeddings cosine, or custom eval score).
- Cost-per-token: aggregated resource accounting for a request normalized to a token. Includes GPU dispatch time, per-kernel execution, and cross-layer overhead (dispatch, serialization).
- Probe SLOs for profiling runs:
  - Measurement noise: standard error of mean (SEM) < 3% across repeated runs.
  - Trace completeness: 100% of kernel boundaries annotated for target traces.
  - Cost correlation: telemetry-derived cost estimate within ±8% of accounting-WAL (billing-derived) for the same window.

Instrumentation contract (signals and semantics)
------------------------------------------------
This contract must be implemented by any runtime or kernel that participates in these experiments. Signals should be emitted using the runtime's telemetry pipeline with the following names and semantics:

- trace.request_id: unique request identifier (UUID).
- trace.model_variant: model name + quantization/precision tag (e.g., gptx2-8bit-v1).
- trace.sequence_len: integer, sequence length processed (input+generated).
- kernel.exec_ms: float, wall-time for the kernel execution in milliseconds.
- kernel.type: enum (attention, ff, matmul, kv_prefetch, decoder-step).
- kernel.queue_wait_ms: float, how long the request waited in scheduler queue.
- scheduler.slot_size: integer, number of requests batched together for that kernel invocation.
- kvcache.hits / kvcache.misses: integer counters for prefix reuse.
- network.serialized_bytes: integer, bytes transferred between runtime shards.
- accounting.gpu_ms: per-GPU accumulated ms attributed to request (derived by sampler).
- metadata.build_id / metadata.kernel_hash: strings to tie traces to binary artifacts.

Each signal must include a timestamp and be taggable with environment (prod/stage), region, and tenant-id (for Dedicated/Private).

Telemetry cardinality table (recommended retention)
--------------------------------------------------
Signal | Cardinality guidance | Reasoning
------ | --------------------- | ---------
trace.request_id | high | Required for trace reconstruction and causal attribution
kernel.exec_ms | high | Primary latency breakdown
kernel.type | medium | Grouping by kernel class for regression cause
scheduler.slot_size | medium | Batching and cost analysis
accounting.gpu_ms | low-medium | Cost reconciliation; sample-based can be used
metadata.* | low | Map to binary and rollout metadata

Profiling experiment matrix (high level)
--------------------------------------
Design experiments to isolate a single variable at a time. Examples:
1) Batch sizing impact on tail latency and per-token cost (vary scheduler.slot_size from 1,2,4,8).
2) Quantization rollout A/B: compare float16 vs 8-bit for the same model variant using identical prompts.
3) KV cache warmup dynamics: measure cold vs warmed kvcache hit rates and perf impact.
4) Kernel handoff regressions: insert synthetic latency into a specific kernel and validate scheduler behavior and cost delta.

For each experiment capture:
- hypothesis (one sentence),
- independent variable(s),
- fixed variables (hardware, sequence length distribution),
- sample size and run duration,
- success criteria (fidelity tolerance, cost delta threshold).

Standardized bench corpus and prompt sets
---------------------------------------
Use the canonical benchmarking corpus located in the benchmarking suite. For fidelity experiments include at minimum:
- 1000 short prompts (0–32 tokens)
- 500 medium prompts (32–256 tokens)
- 200 long prompts (256–1024 tokens)

Always run with deterministic seeds where applicable and capture random-number-generator state in metadata.

Profiling runbook (quick incident triage)
----------------------------------------
Follow these numbered steps when investigating a suspected regression or performing a focused profiling experiment: 
1) Reproduce the symptom in a staging mirror using traffic replay. Document the input corpus, build_id, and kernel_hash.
2) Activate high-fidelity tracing for the affected subset (enable kernel.exec_ms at trace level). Be careful to limit sampling to avoid production overhead.
3) Capture sample traces for 10,000 requests or until SEM target is reached.
4) Run data enrichment pipeline to compute per-request cost estimates and kernel contribution table.
5) Correlate fidelity changes using the canonical prompt set. If fidelity regression is observed, flag applied-ml and create a quality incident.
6) If cost regression without fidelity impact is observed, escalate to kernel-scheduler to review admission and slot accounting.
7) Apply targeted mitigations according to the mitigation table (see below).
8) For any binary/kernel change, run the bench-suite acceptance matrix (see 'Release gating' below) before rolling.

Mitigation table (common symptoms)
----------------------------------
Symptom | Likely cause | Immediate mitigation | Owner
--------|--------------|----------------------|------
Higher per-token GPU ms, no fidelity change | schedule/granularity change or unexpected sloting | Reduce slot_size to emergency smaller bin, throttle low-priority cohorts | kernel-scheduler
High tail latency | kernel queuing or NVLink saturation | Drain NVLink-heavy nodes, reroute traffic, enable backpressure | eng-sre / runtime-ops
Fidelity regression | quantization mismatch, kernel bug, wrong model variant | Roll back kernel binary, revert quantization rollout, engage applied-ml | runtime-release/applied-ml
Large network serialization bytes | sharded state transfer or incorrect serialization path | Enable compact serializer and route to local caches | runtime-network

Kernel scheduler considerations
------------------------------
- Scheduler must annotate slot_size and preemption events in telemetry.
- For reproducible profiling, scheduler should support a deterministic batching mode (fixed window) that can be enabled in staging.
- Provide a scheduler-level 'profiling-token' header that pins low-latency priority and disables best-effort preemption for the duration of the experiment.
- When evaluating new scheduling policies, run the 'slot-synthesis' synthetic workload from the benchmarking suite to validate fairness and cost envelopes.

Benchmarking suite integration
-----------------------------
- Bench runner should accept a --profiling-mode flag that:
  - pins the metadata.build_id and kernel_hash,
  - enables deterministic batching if requested,
  - provisions trace.request_id tags and collects kernel-level metrics.
- Output artifacts:
  - per-experiment metrics.csv with cost and fidelity aggregates,
  - raw-traces.tar.gz (sampled),
  - bench-report.html summarizing deltas and charts.
- Bench artifacts must be uploaded to the experiment storage bucket with a stable naming scheme: {bench}/{build_id}/{experiment_slug}/{timestamp}/

Release gating and signoff checklist
------------------------------------
Before rolling kernel or scheduler changes to production run the following: 
- Run bench-suite acceptance matrix against staging cluster.
- Verify no fidelity regression > 0.5% on canonical prompt set (applied-ml must sign off).
- Verify cost delta per-token within configured threshold (default 5%).
- Ensure tracing metadata is emitted and matches instrumentation contract.
- Confirm rollback automation is wired and smoke tests for connectivity pass.
- Approvers required: kernel-scheduler lead, runtime-observability owner, applied-ml approver.

Known issues (catalog and temporary workarounds)
-----------------------------------------------
- Issue: Sampled accounting.gpu_ms undercounts during mixed-precision kernels.
  - Workaround: Increase sampling rate or enable micro-instrumentation for affected builds.
  - Ticket: #INF-4721
- Issue: scheduler.slot_size unstable under sudden burst traffic leading to queue thrashing.
  - Workaround: engage the emergency admission controller to cap slot_size at 4 and enable backpressure for best-effort cohorts.
  - Ticket: #INF-5033
- Issue: kvcache hits reported but observed fidelity indicates stale cache usage in canary environments.
  - Workaround: purge kvcache on canary instances before experiment.
  - Ticket: #INF-4890

Appendix A: sample commands and example trace enrichment pipeline
-----------------------------------------------------------------
1) Run bench in profiling mode (example):
   ./bench-runner --suite canonical --build-id gptx2-8b-proto --profiling-mode --deterministic-batching --out /tmp/bench-output

2) Enable trace sampling (CLI to control-plane):
   curl -X POST "https://control-plane.internal/api/v1/tracing/sampling" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"rate":0.02, "filters": {"model":"gptx2*"}}'

3) Minimal enrichment pipeline (pseudocode):
   - ingest raw traces from /tmp/bench-output/raw-traces
   - group by trace.request_id, sum kernel.exec_ms, attach accounting.gpu_ms samples
   - compute per-token cost = accounting.gpu_ms / trace.sequence_len
   - join with fidelity evaluation results and output metrics.csv

Appendix B: experiment template (copy/paste)
-------------------------------------------
Title: Quant-AB-test-v2
Hypothesis: 8-bit quant reduces cost by >= 20% with <= 0.5% fidelity regression on canonical short prompts.
Independent variable: model variant (fp16 vs 8bit)
Fixed: same hardware (A100 80GB), traffic shape (50% short,30% mid,20% long), deterministic seeds
Sample size: 20k requests per cohort
Success: cost delta >= 18% and fidelity regression <= 0.5%
Artifacts: metrics.csv, raw-traces.tar.gz, bench-report.html
